title: Flip certificates for odd-period words
claim: Proved by hand: under the plain not-all-equal law along one shift, flipping every value never maps an odd orbit onto itself but forbids nothing (lemma 1); a word satisfies a knot kind through its residue pairs, which for odd periods have distinct residues (lemma 2); a compatible word with a flippable residue rules out every harmony allowing the word (lemma 3); a word of odd period p without such a certificate would make the base of its kinds of span less than p a harmony (lemma 4, suggested by the advisor model). Computer-assisted, refereed by fresh code and by an independent session: every one of the 25,328,938 Lyndon words of odd period 3 to 29 has a certificate, so no not-all-equal harmony at any span and with any number of knot kinds has a state of odd period at most 29. Not proved for every odd period.
failure_conditions: A word of odd period without a certificate (by lemma 4, an odd-period harmony).
A certificate for a word of a known harmony (the control).
The referees disagreeing with the census.
foundation_claim_scope: The plain not-all-equal law on bases along one shift with one distinction per shift; words of odd period 3 to 29.

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the coordinator's go-ahead on 2026-11-12, pre-registered (commit 8f4b693b8); refereed by fresh code (even_referee.py) and by an independent fresh model session (independent_referee/report.md).
validation.status: lemmas by hand; exhaustive census (check.py); both referees passed
